headline: JavaScript Calls Functions Without Parentheses
lede: A runtime hook, coercion, and a little prototype mischief turn an ordinary expression into executable code. It is less a practical idiom than a compact tour of JavaScript’s stranger machinery.

headline: Meta Terms Open the Door to Scraping
lede: Meta’s revised commercial terms appear to grant broad permission to scrape business-linked websites, including news publishers. The legal footing is unsettled; the bargaining power is not.

headline: The Crows Keep Leaving Thank-You Gifts
lede: After helping rescue an injured crow, Lia Wilson began finding feathers and other objects on her walks. Whether the birds mean gratitude or simply remember a useful human, the encounters remain charmingly mysterious.

headline: Meta Opens Its 816-Billion-Parameter Model
lede: Muse Spark Open arrives with 42 billion active parameters, a million-token context window, and open weights for coding and agentic work. Meta also points to an unusually local setup: two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios can run it through MLX.

headline: Mapping Rome’s Economic Complexity
lede: A study turns geocoded Latin inscriptions and occupational records into an estimate of economic complexity across the Western Roman Empire. The result tracks modern regional patterns, while the surviving evidence remains selective and heavily skewed toward elites.

headline: Two Stacks Make Sliding Windows Simple
lede: A pair of stacks supports constant-time aggregate queries and amortized constant-time updates, even when the operation has no inverse. The pattern handles sums, minima, quantiles, and approximate cardinalities without letting old numerical errors linger.

headline: RPKI Now Covers 70% of Internet Routes
lede: Route-origin validation has reached 70.3% of Internet prefixes, up sharply from a year ago. The milestone is real, but broad authorizations and missing records still leave room for leaks and hijacks.

headline: Your Workplace Knows Where the Market Is Going
lede: Employees often see a company’s strengths, failures, and strategic drift before outsiders do. Those signals can guide small career moves—but calling the practice insider trading confuses useful information with securities law.
pullquote: Career intelligence is not insider trading—but it can still change your timing.

headline: Neural Networks May Be Cleaner Than Expected
lede: A new interpretability argument revisits polysemantic neurons and superposition, suggesting that many apparent mixtures reflect meaningful shared structure or weak analysis tools. If the claim holds, researchers may be able to inspect native circuits more directly.

headline: This Programming Language Lives in Folders
lede: Folders encodes programs through directory containment and alphabetical order, treating the filesystem as syntax instead of storage. It is an esolang in the purest sense: carefully implemented, conceptually coherent, and gloriously impractical.
